question: Does the Sandu public record bind a buyer-specific first unprepaid rent receipt and current paid-through cursor strongly enough to convert the apparent 6.90% gross yield into source-bound post-transfer cashflow, or does the causal chain terminate at non-public lease/ledger evidence?

public_sources.title: Current Sandu first-auction notice and investigation table - Jianshe West Road title 11032107
bound_facts: First auction starts 2026-09-25 at RMB 391,374 for the exact 51.16 sqm commercial unit under title certificate 11032107.
The unit is occupied under a lease from 2025-10-05 through 2030-09-30.
Rent is RMB 27,000 per year and is paid semiannually.
The auction notice says the asset is auctioned and delivered in its current condition.
The notice does not state the current paid-through rent date, the first rent cycle payable after transfer, prepaid-rent allocation, tenant identity, deposit or rent ledger.

public_sources.title: PRC Civil Code Article 725 - Supreme People's Court republication
bound_facts: Ownership change during the tenant's contractual possession does not affect lease validity.
This establishes generic lease continuity, not the Sandu case-specific allocation of already-paid rent or the first buyer-side receipt.

public_sources.title: Supreme People's Court network judicial auction rules
bound_facts: Auctioned property ownership transfers when the auction-completion adjudication is served on the buyer.
This narrows the ownership-transfer boundary but does not publish the Sandu case's adjudication date, rent ledger, prepayment balance or first buyer rent settlement.

causal_chain: The observed contractual cashflow is RMB 27,000 per year and the current entry floor is RMB 391,374, producing approximately 6.90% nominal gross before costs.
The lease began 2025-10-05 and uses a semiannual payment cadence, so the surface annual rent alone does not identify how much rent is already paid or prepaid at the time of the 2026-09-25 auction.
Civil Code Article 725 preserves lease validity across ownership change, while the judicial-auction rule places ownership transfer at service of the auction-completion adjudication.
Neither generic legal rule identifies the case-specific first rent amount/date payable to the buyer or allocates any rent already collected by the seller before ownership transfer.
The current Sandu notice itself publishes no paid-through cursor, prepaid-rent allocation, tenant identity, deposit, payment ledger or first buyer-side rent cycle.

To guarantee at least 24 months of source-bound future receipts through the 2030-09-30 lease end, the first buyer-side unprepaid receipt would need to be bound no later than 2028-09-30; the public record does not bind that date because the prepayment/payment cursor is unknown.
Therefore the apparent 6.90% gross yield is not yet a verified buyer cashflow yield: it could only be promoted after the post-transfer receipt start and prepaid-rent accounting are source-bound.

Exact public searches by execution case, title certificate and address surfaced the auction notice and a sibling unit in the same execution case, but no independent lease contract, rent ledger, deposit record or buyer-specific payment settlement.

exact_public_search_exhaustion.note: The current auction notice and generic legal continuity were exhausted without upgrading UNKNOWN buyer receipt fields to PASS.

decisive_unknowns_remaining: Exact current rent paid-through date and any prepaid balance.
Exact first rent amount/date payable to the buyer after ownership transfer.
Treatment of rent collected before transfer for periods extending after transfer.
Tenant identity, payment performance, full lease and deposit.
Utility/property arrears, exact buyer-side taxes/transfer costs, title-transfer timing and physical condition.
